The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has said 78 suspects arrested over the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja are to be freed after the President granted them clemency. The command disclosed this in a statement on Monday by its spokesperson, CSP Josephine Adeh. The police statement marked the first official confirmation of the attack, which was initially disputed by the Presidency. On the day of the incident, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New Media, O’tega Ogra, rejected reports that youths had stoned the President’s convoy at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Garki. In a post accompanying a video showing Tinubu leaving the mosque after Friday prayers, Ogra said, “Contrary to the narrative being pushed by the opposition, with videos of their alleged paid thugs at the National Mosque today, here is footage of Mr President leaving the mosque after Friday prayers this afternoon.” However, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dino Melaye, later shared a video purportedly showing youths throwing stones at a convoy believed to be that of the President. The footage, which went viral on social media, also captured some of the youths chanting “Ba ma yi, ba ma so,” a Hausa expression meaning “we don’t want you; we don’t support you.” Confirming the incident, Adeh said some individuals attacked the President’s convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. “The FCT Police Command wishes to inform the public that 78 suspects were arrested following the attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu, on Friday, November 13, 2026, at a mosque in Garki District, Abuja. “The incident occurred shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in Garki, when some individuals attacked the departing convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and causing injuries to some security operatives,” the statement read. Adeh said a joint security team led by the police responded to the incident, while subsequent intelligence-led raids in the area led to additional arrests, bringing the number of suspects to 78. She added that the Presidency subsequently directed the release of the suspects after extending clemency to them. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Adeh added that the FCT Commissioner of Police, Ahmed Sanusi, warned against violence and destruction of property ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeh quoted the CP as urging political parties, actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful engagement and shun violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and incitement. She added that Sanusi had directed area commanders, divisional police officers and heads of tactical units to intensify security operations to ensure the safety of residents and visitors. Kano police arrest 8 The Kano State police command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Bichi Local Government Area of the state. The police said five people sustained injuries while 13 vehicles were vandalised during the violence, which occurred at about 4:45 pm on Sunday. The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa. “The clash also led to the destruction of campaign banners and billboards belonging to the political parties,” the statement said. State police: NASS confirms all 36 assemblies approve bill Tinubu’s education reforms yielding results – Minister Tinubu tightens security, 128 police chiefs redeployed It said police teams were immediately deployed to the area after receiving a report of the incident, adding that their intervention restored calm. “Items recovered from the suspects included one Gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, a bottle of solution and a substance locally known as ‘Suck and Die’,” the police said. The five injured persons were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment, the statement added. The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Bakori, condemned the violence and destruction of campaign materials by political supporters, warning that the command would not tolerate activities capable of threatening public peace. “I’m urging political parties and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law,” the commissioner said. The statement said the suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai, Kano, for investigation and would be charged in court upon its conclusion. The command urged political leaders, party supporters and residents to shun violence and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. It added that the area remained relatively calm, while security monitoring continued. PUNCH Online earlier on Monday reported that suspected thugs had attacked the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. In a post on his verified X account on Monday, the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, confirmed the incident and said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. He described Kwankwaso as his brother and running mate in the 2027 presidential election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress. “I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. “I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor warned against using political differences as justification for violence, intimidation and destruction of property. He stressed that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack, regardless of political affiliation. Obi urged the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those responsible, including alleged sponsors, and ensure they were brought to justice. He also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC and others affected by the incident, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery. “Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence. “Nigeria belongs to all of us. We may belong to different political parties, but we remain one people with a common destiny. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” he added. Kindly share this story:
